name: Speciality Restaurants Ltd
title: Speciality Restaurants Ltd - 534425 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Restaurant operator with revenue up 18.2% to INR 129.78 crores and same-store sales up 8.1% in Q2; no supply-side discipline signals, and the call does not revisit the prior FY27 store-addition or cash guidance.

summary.headline: Speciality Restaurants Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18.24% YoY to INR 129.78 crore, with operational EBITDA up 39.44% to INR 10.24 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 18.24% YoY to INR 129.78 crore and PAT rose 45.75% to INR 6.94 crore. Operational EBITDA margin expanded to 8.03% from 6.81%, and same-store sales growth was 8.1% in Q2 (11.32% in Q1; 9.8% in H1). Delivery mix rose to 32% from 27.4% a year earlier, and the network stood at 125 outlets at September 30, 2026. Management flagged a pipeline of 2-3 openings in Q3 and a 200-outlet target by FY2030, with restaurant-level EBITDA of 22-23% post Ind AS as the internal benchmark.

financial_highlights.change: +18.24% YoY vs INR 109.76 crore in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Company-level EBITDA margin (pre Ind AS, ex lease accounting)

financial_highlights.value: 32% of Q2 FY27 sales (management also cited ~29% elsewhere in call)

segments.name: Asia Kitchen (illustrative unit economics)
segments.commentary: Monthly throughput of INR 60-75 lakh (about INR 2-2.5 lakh per day), gross margin ~76%, staff cost 20-22%, rentals 18%, opex 11%, restaurant EBITDA ~22%, depreciation 4%, restaurant-level profit ~18%.

segments.name: Network by brand
segments.commentary: 125 outlets at September 30, 2026: 118 company-owned and operated plus 7 franchise-owned company-operated (including one under a subsidiary). Brands: Mainland China, Asia Kitchen (mall format), Gong (premium Asian), Haka (delivery), Siciliana (Italian all-day cafe), Sweet Bengal (sweets, QSR), Walters (burgers, QSR).

guidance_outlook: Target of about 200 physical outlets by FY2030 (excluding kitchen-within-kitchen units); current count was 207 per the question, versus 125 outlets stated by management, which needs reconciliation.
Restaurant-level EBITDA target of 22-23% post Ind AS for new restaurants.
Revenue growth expected at about 20-22% a year from new openings and existing stores.
Capex of about INR 4-5 crore per restaurant; roughly INR 50 crore spend per year, with management expecting the business to become cash flow positive in coming years.
Q3 FY27: 2 new Gong openings (Delhi, Pune Koregaon Park), 3 Walters openings, and one more Siciliana, taking Gong to 4 and Siciliana to about 6 outlets.
Delivery mix expected to reach 30-35% over 2-3 years, with dine-in growing alongside.
capex_capacity: H2 FY27 openings planned across Mumbai, Delhi, Pune, Bangalore, Kolkata and Dubai, alongside renovations and brand conversions at select existing sites.
Gong re-entry into Delhi this quarter; expansion focus shifts to Delhi, Hyderabad and Bangalore alongside existing core markets of West Bengal, Mumbai, Bangalore and Pune.
Capex of about INR 50 crore a year; management said per-restaurant spend is INR 4-5 crore.
Kitchen-within-kitchen model lets one unit serve multiple brands (e.g., Mainland China, Asia Kitchen, Haka) with no extra capex or staff cost, giving three points of sale from one kitchen.
demand_pricing: Delivery is structural: management described a shift to a hybrid model in which dine-in is occasional and delivery lets brands reach consumers about 4 times a week; aggregator offers and campaigns are used to drive delivery.
Per aggregator data, about 75% of delivery customers are new to the brands and 25% are loyal customers (management does not track delivery customer data directly).
Price increases have been limited; management attributed margin protection to vendor renegotiation and buying power from multi-chain, multi-brand scale and future unit commitments.
Conversions of Mainland China to Asia Kitchen reportedly grew sales 25-30%; management targets same-store growth of 10-15% for Oriental brands.
Q3 is seasonally the strongest quarter; seasonal and marketing plans are in place.

qa_highlights.question: Company-level EBITDA and margin on pre-Ind AS basis (ex lease accounting)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said company-level EBITDA margin was 7.90% in Q2 FY27 versus 6.52% a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Unit economics for Asia Kitchen, Mainland China, Gong and Walters?
qa_highlights.answer: For Asia Kitchen, monthly throughput is INR 60-75 lakh (INR 2-2.5 lakh per day), with restaurant-level EBITDA of about 22% and restaurant-level profit of about 18% after 4% depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for the seasonally strong next quarter and new openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is optimistic on Q3 with 2-3 new restaurants launching, including 2 Gong, 3 Walters and 1 Siciliana.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term delivery mix and how the company will grow customer reach?
qa_highlights.answer: Delivery is about 29-30% of business and is expected to reach 30-35%; growth will come through kitchen-within-kitchen formats and aggregator campaigns.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material inflation and margins managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not taken a large price hike and has relied on vendor renegotiation and scale-based buying power.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for the 200-outlet target by FY2030 and per-outlet economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is mainly physical outlets across the Oriental, Siciliana and QSR brands; target restaurant EBITDA is 22-23% post Ind AS and revenue growth of 20-22%.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of rising delivery mix on margins (QSR lens)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dine-in growth should offset delivery cost pressure, so net margins should improve; 70% of business is dine-in based.

qa_highlights.question: Capex per restaurant and funding from operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-restaurant capex is INR 4-5 crore, roughly INR 50 crore a year; management expects the business to turn cash flow positive in future years.

risks_watch: Delivery mix growth may dilute restaurant margins; management's claim that dine-in growth offsets this is unverified.
Raw material inflation: price increases are limited, so margin protection depends on vendor terms.
Execution risk on about INR 50 crore annual capex and the 200-outlet FY2030 target; the outlet count (125 vs 207) needs clarification.
Same-store sales growth decelerated from 11.32% in Q1 to 8.1% in Q2.
Operating cash flow of roughly INR 50 crore cited by an analyst; cash flow positivity is pitched for future years only.
Entry into Delhi, Hyderabad and Bangalore and new brand conversions carry ramp-up risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, delivery and expansion, with clear quantified targets. Less specific on margin pressure from delivery and on the outlet count, and some answers were deferred or partial (e.g., competitor brand comparisons declined).
key_quotes: What we have witnessed during this particular quarter is the same-store sales growth which had been 8.1% in the quarter 2, which was 11.32% in quarter 1 and is 9.8% in H1 of FY27.

This is a complete trend because we've seen a complete shift of diner habits to more of a hybrid model where dine-in is something that people feel is achievable may be probably once a week or twice in a month.

The best plan that has worked magically for us is kitchen within kitchen concepts, where, for example, if we have an Asian kitchen, we also do deliver our other Asian brands from the very same kitchen without having any extra capex or staff costs or any other costs added to it.

adds.what: 2 new Gong openings (Delhi, Pune Koregaon Park), 3 Walters openings and 1 Siciliana in Q3 FY27 (Gong to 4, Siciliana to about 6 outlets)
H2 FY27 restaurant openings across Mumbai, Delhi, Pune, Bangalore, Kolkata and Dubai, plus renovations and brand conversions
Target of about 200 physical outlets by FY2030 (ex kitchen-within-kitchen), capex about INR 50 crore a year at INR 4-5 crore per restaurant

growth.why: Management guides revenue growth of about 20-22% a year, backed by specific Q3 openings (2 Gong, 3 Walters, 1 Siciliana) and H2 FY27 openings across six cities, with per-restaurant capex of INR 4-5 crore and about INR 50 crore a year, though no order book or unit-level timeline beyond this is given.
